newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: U.S. oil majors to sign Venezuela deal July 9.
newsitem.headline: U.S. oil majors to sign Venezuela deal July 9.

text.p: ARCO, Texaco Inc and Phillips Petroleum Corp are due to sign their $3.5 billion extra-heavy oil venture with Venezuela's state oil subsidiary Corpoven on July 9, a Corpoven official said Thursday.

The Hamaca venture in Venezuela's Orinoco Oil Belt has already been approved by Congress and the signing would mark the beginning of the basic engineering phase. The project aims to produce 200,000 barrels per day (bpd) of extra-heavy crude and build a deep-conversion plant to convert it into something resembling traditional crude oil.
Phillips has said the group intends to spend $110 million in the first 18 months of the contract.
Hamaca is one of five signed Orinoco projects although four more are in various stages of negotiation.

A similar venture between Venezuela's Maraven and Conoco recently issued a $1 billion bond on international markets, and Corpoven too expected a bond offering. Up to 60 percent of the venture will be funded through debt, a Corpoven official said.

The Hamaca partners are planning to share electricity, water, pipelines and port facilities with three other projects in the western Oil Belt, resulting in total savings of about $1 billion, he added. The other projects in that area are one comprising Lagoven, Mobil and Veba, a second with Corpoven and Exxon, and a third including Maraven, Total, Norsk Hydro and Statoil.
The $320 million contract to build the port facilities in the northern town of Jose was expected to be announced in a month's time, the official said.

The pipeline carrying the 660,000 bpd planned output from the four projects would be built, owned and operated by a third party which would charge a tariff based on use. A tender for this $140 million contract would be announced in the third quarter of this year, the official said.
